newsitem.title: UK: EMS/Mark eases in Europe, shrugs off soft dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: EMS/Mark eases in Europe, shrugs off soft dlr/mark.

text.p: The mark was steady on its European crosses in afternoon Europe but kept to the bottom of session ranges despite a late retreat in dollar/mark.

Dollar strength early in the session put the mark on the defensive against its European satellites while growing market sentiment for a broad-based, timely start to Europe's monetary union was seen capping any mark gains.

New estimates of Germany's 1997 tax revenue are due Thursday. German coalition sources said revenue will be just under 20 billion marks less than expected. The federal budget foresees a deficit of 53.4 billion marks.

"Germany will not likely meet the three percent deficit target," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London. "The market seems to be taking the path of a flexible interpretation of the EMU criteria."

Bundesbank member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said earlier today Germany's 1997 budget deficit could 3.2-3.3 percent of GDP, above the EMU threshold of 3.0 percent. Earlier, Bundesbank member Ernst Welteke's comments the dollar at 1.70 marks was justified by fundamentals pressured the mark on its crosses. His other comments that the 3.0 percent EMU deficit target was less important than sustaining low deficit levels had less of an impact but did provide some cross support.

However, analysts said the emphasis seemed to be on sustaining low deficits and took it as a reference to Italy after Monday's Ecofin report calling for more sustainable measures by Italy to control its spending.

"Everyone knows what the German attitude to Italy in EMU is. A trader would have to have a pretty short memory to buy the lira on this story," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International in London.
Nevertheless, mark/lira lost ground, testing close to four-week lows earlier. By 1430 GMT, it was trading at 984.80/5.00 per mark from 988.50/9.00 late Tuesday.
Analysts said the lira was benefiting from gains in the peseta and escudo against the mark, both fuelled by mild inflation data and the prospect of lower rates.
"The Spanish CPI was good and a rate cut is expected and now speculation is for the Bank of Italy to follow suit," said First Chicago's Knuthsen.
Spanish April CPI came in at 1.7 percent year-on-year against 1.9 percent forecast and 2.2 percent in March. Expectations are high the Bank of Spain will trim it repo rate as early as this Friday.

Mark/peseta stood at 84.42/43 after touching a session low of 84.35 but still below late Tuesday's 84.48/49 pesetas. Mark/escudo was weaker at 100.53/56, above session lows but just down from 100.57/60 Tuesday.
The French franc was also firmer, supported by the ruling centre-right maintaining its lead in the latest opinion polls ahead of the forthcoming French election.
Robust February current account data was also seen helping, coming in well above expectations at 19.2 billion francs.
Mark/French franc was trading at 3.3676/78 against 3.3681/86 Tuesday.

The Swedish crown traded firmer in late trade, maintaining its trend higher throughout the session. Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said earlier the government would announce its view on EMU before the end of May and dismissed press reports that the government took a negative view of the single currency project.
Mark/crown stood at 4.4715/45 against 4.5100/30 late Tuesday.
